original-data.t: The six customers as they are: usage across and monthly spend up. PCA will find a **better set of axes** for the same points.

center.t: Subtracting the feature means **(4.5, 3.5)** moves the center of the cloud to the origin, because PCA describes the spread around the center.

principal-axis.t: **PC1** (solid yellow) follows the cloud. **PC2** (dashed blue) is perpendicular to it. Together they are a rotated set of axes for the same data.

project.t: Each point is dropped perpendicularly onto PC1. The projected positions are what we will keep.

pc1-coordinate.t: The labels give each customer's **position along PC1**, from **−3.20** for the lowest to **3.53** for the highest. These are the new, single coordinates.

drop-pc2.t: The red segments are the **PC2 coordinates**: each customer's distance from the PC1 line. They are all small (at most 0.61), so dropping them loses little.

one-dimensional-data.t: The data is now **six numbers on a line**, the PC1 coordinates, with the same order and spacing as along the trend.

compare-representations.t: Two numbers per customer keep everything (**100% of the variance**). One number per customer keeps **97.2%** while storing half as much.

pca-summary.t: **Center, find the directions of greatest variance, keep the top coordinates.** PC1 is a **new feature** that mixes both originals, so PCA is not the same as picking a column.
